name: EcoGalaxy

seo.title: EcoGalaxy Catamaran Galapagos: Cruises | James Wild & Co
seo.description: EcoGalaxy, Galaxy Cruises' 16-guest First Class catamaran with 8 cabins and a 360-degree sundeck. 4 and 5-night Southern, Western and Northern routes.

tagline: A First Class catamaran for 16, built with sustainability in mind.
answer: EcoGalaxy is Galaxy Cruises' First Class expedition catamaran for 16 guests in 8 cabins, with 9 crew, a cruise director and one bilingual naturalist guide. Galaxy describes her as a sustainable catamaran using 50% less wood than a conventional vessel. She sails 4-night Southern and 5-night Western and Northern routes, from US$4,100 per person in 2026. Children from 6.
facts: Southern 4 nights, Western 5 nights, Northern 5 nights
overview: EcoGalaxy is a twin-hull expedition catamaran run by Galaxy Cruises, which calls her a First Class sustainable catamaran. Galaxy says she uses 50% less wood than a conventional vessel and lists LED lighting, recycled materials, smart climate control and water purification and recirculation.
She takes 16 guests in eight cabins. Shared spaces include a 360-degree sundeck, an open-air deck, social lounges, a bar and a boutique. Kayaks, paddleboards, snorkel gear and wetsuits are on board.

The 4-night Southern Route runs from San Cristobal to Baltra via Espanola, Floreana, Santa Fe and South Plaza. The 5-night Western Route loops from Baltra through Isabela, Fernandina and Santiago. The 5-night Northern Route runs Baltra to San Cristobal via Rabida, North Seymour, Genovesa and Bartolome.
why: A First Class price on a catamaran, with sustainability written into the build.
The three routes chain by day of the week: Southern, Western and Northern together make 14 nights without repeating a route.

pricesNote: Per person, cruise only, USD, as published on galaxycruises.com/ecogalaxy-catamaran on 2 Nov 2026, labelled 2026 price: Southern (4 nights) US$4,100, Western and Northern (5 nights) US$5,100. Occupancy basis not stated. Dated departures were not captured: Galaxy's booking feed loads in the browser and could not be read on 2 Nov 2026. Galaxy publishes 2026 itinerary prices only on the yacht page; 2027 prices are not published there.
inclusions: Airport assistance on the cruise start date
Cruise director and personalised crew service
All meals from lunch on day one to breakfast on the last day
A snack after each activity (except the last day) and a welcome cocktail
Unlimited purified water, coffee and tea
All visits, excursions and activities in the itinerary
Snorkel gear (mask, snorkel, fins) and wetsuits
Airport to canal and canal to airport transport (Lobitos bus)
Kayaks and paddleboards in authorised areas
exclusions: International flights to and from Ecuador
Flights between Quito or Guayaquil and the Galapagos
Galapagos National Park entrance fee, US$200 per person
Transit Control Card, US$20 per person
Travel insurance (Galaxy calls it highly recommended)
children: Galaxy says EcoGalaxy welcomes children from 6 years old; there is no babysitting, so families should check the itinerary activities. Galaxy Cruises' terms accept children over 6 on shared departures and children of any age on a full charter; under-12s share a cabin with an adult or sleep in a cabin next to their parents. The booking form prices children aged 6 to 11 separately.
faqs: How many guests does EcoGalaxy carry?
Sixteen, in eight cabins, with nine crew, a cruise director and one bilingual naturalist guide.
Galaxy says she uses 50% less wood than a conventional vessel, with LED lighting, recycled materials, smart climate control and water purification and recirculation.
A 4-night Southern Route from San Cristobal, a 5-night Western Route from Baltra and a 5-night Northern Route ending at San Cristobal.
How much does an EcoGalaxy cruise cost?
Galaxy's 2026 prices are US$4,100 per person for the Southern Route and US$5,100 for the Western or Northern Route. Flights and park fees are extra.
Yes, from 6 years old. There is no babysitting on board.
Galaxy lists EcoGalaxy as First Class, a step below its Luxury catamarans Alya and Galaxy Sirius.
Galaxy's booking form offers a whole-boat charter; the price is quoted on request.
Meals, snacks, water, coffee and tea, guided excursions, snorkel gear, wetsuits, kayaks and paddleboards, and airport assistance. Drinks, tips, flights and park fees are extra.
